configuration.limitation: Law on Social Insurance 41/2024/QH15 art.33 and art.34 — 8% employee and 17.5% employer, on a salary capped at 20 times the statutory reference level (2,530,000, ceiling 50,600,000). The employer 17.5% is 3% sickness and maternity, 14% retirement and survivorship, and 0.5% occupational accident and disease under the Law on Occupational Safety and Hygiene 84/2015/QH13 art.44 with Decree 58/2020/NĐ-CP art.4. Floor: Luật BHXH 41/2024/QH15 Điều 31(1)(đ) — tiền lương làm căn cứ đóng thấp nhất bằng mức tham chiếu (2,530,000 đ on this version). an employer granted the reduced 0.3% occupational-accident rate (Decree 58/2020 art.5) records the entity fact `occupational_accident_reduced`; its share is then 17.3%. Law 41/2024/QH15 art.31(1)(b) with Decree 158/2025/NĐ-CP art.7(1)(a)–(c): the insurance salary is the monthly job or title wage, plus the wage allowances and the other supplements of a stated amount agreed in the contract and paid regularly and stably each pay period, excluding items that depend on or vary with productivity, work history or performance (`terms.fixed_allowances`, the standing rows marked fixed); a row marked not fixed stays outside. Circular 06/2021/TT-BLĐTBXH, cited here before, was repealed from 1 July 2025 by Circular 12/2025/TT-BNV art.20(2)(b). Above the ceiling (twenty times the reference level) the employer’s share is the ceiling at the employer’s own rate — 17.3% where the occupational-accident fund is reduced (Decree 58/2020 art.4), 17.5% otherwise — the same choice the open rungs make. The base recorded is the insurance salary itself — the contractual salary floored at the reference level (2530000.0) and capped at twenty times it (50600000.0) — so a scheme that reads `produced.SI.base` reads the insured salary. Unpaid-leave continuation: Law 41/2024/QH15 arts.33(5) and 34(3) permit continuation by agreement at the most recent contribution base; art.31(1)(đ) sets the bounds at contribution time. The dated registration records the agreement, reference and prior base. Decree 158/2025/NĐ-CP art.43(2) retains occupational-accident contributions on the compulsory SI salary. https://xaydungchinhsach.chinhphu.vn/toan-van-luat-so-41-2024-qh15-bao-hiem-xa-hoi-119240723163650489.htm https://xaydungchinhsach.chinhphu.vn/toan-van-nghi-dinh-158-2025-nd-cp-quy-dinh-ve-bao-hiem-xa-hoi-bat-buoc-119250629171336803.htm Law 41/2024/QH15 art.33(5) limits the unpaid-month waiver to the listed categories, excluding part-time employees under art.2(1)(l); art.33(6) requires SI in the first working or return month with at least 14 sickness-benefit working days. Benefit eligibility and return-month status are dated declarations. BHXH letter 371/BHXH-QLT of 7 July 2025 section 1.2 counts a paid half-day as a working day; the threshold counts fully unpaid working dates, not summed wage-deduction fractions. https://cdn.thuvienphapluat.vn/uploads/Hoidapphapluat/2025/LNMT/Thang_7/250707/QLT-%C4%90VSDL%C4%90.pdf Maternity contributions: Law 41/2024/QH15 art.53(8) exempts birth, adoption under six months, surrogate-birth and commissioning-mother benefit leave without imposing 14 working days; other maternity-benefit cases are exempt only from 14 working days in the month. The dated eligibility and category elections distinguish statutory benefit leave from ordinary unpaid absence. Article 53(1), Circular 12/2025/TT-BNV art.9(4)(c) require compulsory SI after an early return from birth leave while the maternity allowance continues. Official application (birth leave starting 14 August 2025 is exempt that month): https://chinhsachonline.chinhphu.vn/xac-dinh-thoi-gian-lam-viec-de-dong-bhxh-82176.htm Circular: https://xaydungchinhsach.chinhphu.vn/toan-van-thong-tu-12-2025-tt-bnv-quy-dinh-chi-tiet-mot-so-dieu-cua-luat-bhxh-ve-bhxh-bat-buoc-11925070415595016.htm Law 41/2024/QH15 art.2(7)(b) — a domestic worker (lao động là người giúp việc gia đình, `employment.type` DOMESTIC) is not a compulsory participant, so the SI base, and the union fund that reads it, is nil for one. Law 41/2024 art.2(2)(b): a foreign employee at retirement age is measured at the contract’s signing against the age Decree 135/2020 art.4 sets for that year (men 60y3m in 2021 rising 3 months a year to 62 in 2028; women 55y4m in 2021 rising 4 months a year to 60 in 2035), read on `employment.service_start`. Law 41/2024/QH15 art.2(1)(a) covers a fixed-term contract only “từ đủ 01 tháng trở lên”; a fixed-term contract of under one full month (`employment.contract_months` < 1) is outside SI, so its base is nothing and the union fee and dues that read `produced.SI.base` follow; the employer owes the worker the equivalent with the wage (Labour Code art.168(3), `INSURANCE_EQUIVALENT`). Decree 135/2020/NĐ-CP art.4 with Annex I (signed text https://datafiles.chinhphu.vn/cpp/files/vbpq/2020/11/135.signed.pdf pp.1–3, read visually) sets the retirement age by the month and year of birth — the age of the year in which the worker reaches it (a man born 7/1964 retires at 61y3m in 10/2025) — so the foreign-worker retirement exclusion compares the age at signing with the Annex I age for `employee.birth_date`, not with the age of the signing year. Engine: the insurance salary is floored at the reference level 2,530,000 and capped at 50,600,000 (20 × the reference level). An employer with the entity fact occupational_accident_reduced pays 17.3%; every other employer 17.5%. Engine: a month with 14 or more unpaid working days (period.unpaid_working_days) charges nothing (Law 41/2024 art.33(5)) unless the SI election unpaid_leave_continuation records the agreement to continue. Engine (round 7): the base is the contractual monthly wage — terms.base_salary plus the term's fixed allowances other than meal, housing and the insurance equivalent (Law 41/2024 art.31(1)(b); Decree 158/2025 art.7) — assessed every salary month even when unpaid days reduce the pay (assess_without_wage); a part-time employee's base is the pay of the month (Decree 158/2025 art.7(2)) and one paid below 2,530,000 is outside compulsory SI and UI (Law 41/2024 art.2(1)(l)). Nothing is charged for a pensioner, a domestic worker, a fixed-term contract under one month, or a foreign employee on a contract under 12 months, an intra-company transferee, one at retirement age at signing (Decree 135/2020 art.4 normal-conditions ages by signing year) or one a treaty exempts (SI election si_treaty_exempt) — Law 41/2024 art.2(2), (7). A month with 14 or more working days unpaid or outside the employment is not charged (art.33(5)) unless the SI election unpaid_leave_continuation records the agreement; sick days do not count in the first or the return month (art.33(6)); a month on maternity leave is not charged (art.53(8)). https://xaydungchinhsach.chinhphu.vn/toan-van-luat-so-41-2024-qh15-bao-hiem-xa-hoi-119240723163650489.htm The month's contribution is charged with the month's regular pay (re-verification 3, 2026-10-22): an off-cycle slip paid before the salary run pays no wage this scheme assesses and charges nothing, so a small bonus or claim slip is never consumed by the month's insurance. The phone, stationery, travel and uniform support (WORK_EXPENSE_ALLOWANCE) is a welfare support outside the insurance salary (Circular 10/2020/TT-BLĐTBXH art.3(5)(c); Official Letter 1198/CTL&BHXH-BHXH of 2025 under Decree 158/2025/NĐ-CP art.7), as its counts_toward already says.

configuration.limitation: Law 109/2025/QH15, Decree 253/2026/ND-CP and Circular 87/2026/TT-BTC (in force 1 July 2026, resident salary from tax period 2026; its art.6(2) replaces Circular 111/2013/TT-BTC) for the 2026 rules; Personal Income Tax Law 04/2007/QH12 and Circular 111/2013/TT-BTC only where this text contrasts the earlier rule. Declared non-residents receive 20% withholding on taxable remuneration without resident personal, dependant or insurance deductions; that rule precedes the resident short-contract withholding rule and does not require a rate override. Resident progressive withholding uses the version’s monthly scale and deduction amounts; the configured year-end rule reconciles annual withholding. Before 1 July 2026, non-residents retain the earlier overtime-premium exemption and taxable leave cash-out. The full qualifying overtime and statutory cessation leave exemptions apply to residents from tax year 2026 and non-residents from 1 July 2026 (Decree 253/2026 arts.26 and 69). A future departure does not establish cessation in the current period. Payments beyond statutory limits remain taxable. Special tax profiles require further verification. Tax residence is a fact the employer records: a resident is present 183 days in the calendar year or twelve months from arrival, or has a registered permanent residence or a rented home for 183 days or more (Decree 253/2026 art.4), and anyone else is non-resident (art.5); neither the Law nor the decree presumes either for an unknown residence, so an unrecorded residence stops the calculation (`terms.tax_residency`). Residence governs the whole tax period (art.66(1)(a): the calendar year, or the first twelve months from arrival): each month is withheld on the status recorded for it (art.46(3), art.64(4): income is taxed when paid), and a change of status during the year is settled in the annual finalisation, which re-prices the year’s wage income on the resident table and credits what was withheld at 20% (art.51; Decree 126/2020 art.8(6)(d)); earlier months are never re-withheld. Leave cash-out: art.26(2) exempts the pay for untaken leave only within the Labour Code art.113(3) conditions and rate (the Decree 145/2020 art.67(3) day), and art.26(3) taxes the excess; income is taxed in the month it is paid (art.46(3)), so an excess is income of the paying month and is never spread over earlier periods. Meal: Decree 253/2026 art.8(2)(g) with art.69(1)(b) — from 1 July 2026 a meal paid by the employer is taxable only above 1,200,000 a month; a meal served in kind is not income. A class counting toward PIT.MEAL enters the base only above that cap. Housing: rent, power and water the employer pays on the worker’s behalf is taxable at the amount paid but not above 15% of the worker’s other taxable income at the unit (Decree 253/2026 art.8(2)(h)); a class counting toward PIT.HOUSING enters at the lower of the two. Voluntary pension and life insurance: deducted as paid, at most 3,000,000 a month in total including the employer’s share, from tax year 2026 (Decree 253/2026 art.46(2)(a) with art.69(1)(a)), read from the dated VOLUNTARY_PENSION deduction claims; the annual settlement allows twelve months’ cap: art.69(1)(a) applies the salary-income rules from tax period 2026, so the December finalisation caps every 2026 month at 3,000,000, January–June included, and art.70(2) settles the months withheld under the old rule in that finalisation (signed text pp.56–57, read 2026-10-08 https://datafiles.chinhphu.vn/cpp/files/vbpq/2026/7/253m-ndcp.signed.pdf). The art.49 medical, education and charity deductions are not withheld monthly: a taxpayer who claims them settles with the tax office personally (Decree 253/2026 art.51(3)), so the employer never applies them. Year-end: the December re-pricing on the annual table is the employer’s finalisation, which it may make only for an employee who authorised it and qualifies (Decree 126/2020 art.8(6)(d); Decree 253/2026 art.51(2)): the PIT election `finalisation_authorised`. Without it December is withheld on the monthly table. Night work: Decree 253/2026 art.26(1) exempts "tiền lương, tiền công làm việc ban đêm" — the wage for night work itself, where Circular 111/2013 art.3(1)(i) exempted only "phần tiền lương, tiền công trả cao hơn" the day wage; Decree 145/2020 art.56 prices the night-work wage as the ordinary hour × night hours plus at least 30% of it. The ordinary night hours' share of the salary (`NIGHT_WAGE`) leaves the base beside the premium for every employee. Engine: Law 109/2025/QH15 art.29(2) — the five-rung monthly scale applies to salary income from the 2026 tax period (5% to 10,000,000; 10% to 30,000,000; 20% to 60,000,000; 30% to 100,000,000; 35% above); Resolution 110/2025/UBTVQH15 — personal deduction 15,500,000 and 6,200,000 per registered dependant a month from the 2026 tax period. Taxable income is the month's PIT base less the employee's compulsory SI 8% + HI 1.5% (and UI 1% for a citizen) computed on the same base within the insurance floor and caps — exact for a salary-only month, an over-deduction in a month carrying a bonus outside the insurance salary — less the personal and dependant deductions. Dependants are the PIT election dependants — the dependants registered with the tax authority (scheme.elections.dependants). Non-residents: 20% of taxable income, no deductions. Insurance deducted is the employee's compulsory SI, HI and UI actually charged in the month (charged.month), exact in a bonus month (Law 109/2025/QH15 art.8(2); Law 04/2007 art.15 before 2026). From 1 July 2026 (Decree 253/2026/NĐ-CP): employee contributions to supplementary or voluntary pension and life insurance are deducted up to 3,000,000 a month (art.46(2)(a); PIT election voluntary_pension_contribution); a resident with no contract or one under three months (employment.start_date to exit_date) is withheld 10% on a payment of 5,000,000 or more, nothing below it or with the commitment form (art.50(2); election commitment_form). Engine (round 7): the meal allowance is taxable only above 1,200,000 a month (Decree 253/2026 art.8(2)(g)); housing the employer pays is taxable up to 15% of the other taxable income (Decree 253/2026 art.8(2)(h)); employer pension/life-insurance contributions are taxable and, with the employee's own, deducted up to 3,000,000 a month (Decree 253/2026 art.46(2)(a)). A resident with no labour contract (employment_type SERVICE) or one under three months is withheld 10% on a payment of 5,000,000 or more (Decree 253/2026 art.50(2)), nothing below it or with the commitment form. December finalises the year for an employee who authorised it (PIT election finalisation_authorised): the annual table (Law 109/2025 art.9) on the year's assessed income less the year's insurance and twelve months' deductions, less the tax already withheld (Decree 253/2026 art.51). A net-of-tax contract (term fact net_of_tax) has the employer bear the tax, grossed up bracket by bracket on the converted income (Circular 111/2013 art.7 and Annex 02). December finalisation (re-verification 2): the year’s pension deduction is the sum of each month the employment paid PIT this year (earned.months), each capped at that month’s limit (1,000,000 before July 2026, 3,000,000 from July; Decree 253/2026 art.46(2)(a)), plus December’s; the employee’s own contribution is read from the standing in force in December (the standing has no monthly history). The dependant deduction counts each dependant from the month registered (election dependants_registered_from, one YYYY-MM each; Circular 111/2013 art.9(1)(c)); without it the registered count is taken for the whole year. Statutory is never deferred (re-verification 3, 2026-10-22): an off-cycle slip paid before the month's salary run is taxed on the month's regular pay still to come (person.normal_pending: the contract wage taxable this month, and person.insurance_pending: the compulsory insurance it bears) plus the extra it pays, less the tax on that regular pay alone, so the slip that pays a bonus carries the tax the bonus attracts; the salary run charges the rest of the month. The short-contract 10% is withheld per payment (each slip on its own) as the threshold is per payment ("/lần").

references.title: Decree 253/2026/NĐ-CP art.26(1) (from 1 July 2026): the wage for night work itself is exempt, not only the part paid above the day wage (Circular 111/2013 art.3(1)(i) before). The normal-hour wage of each normal (non-overtime) hour worked between rules.night_window (the night hours of the paid intervals less those of the overtime intervals) (22:00–06:00) leaves the PIT base; the salary still pays it (an EMPLOYER line is not paid again), and the night premium (NIGHT_WORK) and night overtime are already outside PIT. Decree 145/2020 art.56: the night-work wage is the normal hour wage × night hours plus at least 30%. https://datafiles.chinhphu.vn/cpp/files/vbpq/2026/7/253m-ndcp.signed.pdf Only a normal working day’s night hours (day_type WORK, not a holiday): night hours on a rest day or holiday are paid inside REST_DAY_OVERTIME and HOLIDAY_WORK, which already count toward nothing (Decree 253/2026 art.26(1)), so they are not taken out of PIT a second time. Wage base: Decree 145/2020/NĐ-CP art.55(1)(a) (and art.56 for night work) prices the premium on the actual wage for the work, which leaves out only overtime, night and holiday pay, bonuses and the meal, fuel, phone, travel, housing, childcare and other supports unrelated to the job; the job-related wage allowances (phụ cấp lương, Labour Code art.90(1)) stay in. The hour wage is therefore terms.base_salary plus the contract’s FIXED_ALLOWANCE lines; meal, housing, work-expense and insurance-equivalent classes stay out. https://datafiles.chinhphu.vn/cpp/files/vbpq/2020/12/145.signed.pdf p.41

references.title: Law 109/2025/QH15, Decree 253/2026/ND-CP and Circular 87/2026/TT-BTC (in force 1 July 2026, resident salary from tax period 2026; its art.6(2) replaces Circular 111/2013/TT-BTC) for the 2026 rules; Personal Income Tax Law 04/2007/QH12 and Circular 111/2013/TT-BTC only where this text contrasts the earlier rule. Declared non-residents receive 20% withholding on taxable remuneration without resident personal, dependant or insurance deductions; that rule precedes the resident short-contract withholding rule and does not require a rate override. Resident progressive withholding uses the version’s monthly scale and deduction amounts; the configured year-end rule reconciles annual withholding. Before 1 July 2026, non-residents retain the earlier overtime-premium exemption and taxable leave cash-out. The full qualifying overtime and statutory cessation leave exemptions apply to residents from tax year 2026 and non-residents from 1 July 2026 (Decree 253/2026 arts.26 and 69). A future departure does not establish cessation in the current period. Payments beyond statutory limits remain taxable. Special tax profiles require further verification. Tax residence is a fact the employer records: a resident is present 183 days in the calendar year or twelve months from arrival, or has a registered permanent residence or a rented home for 183 days or more (Decree 253/2026 art.4), and anyone else is non-resident (art.5); neither the Law nor the decree presumes either for an unknown residence, so an unrecorded residence stops the calculation (`terms.tax_residency`). Residence governs the whole tax period (art.66(1)(a): the calendar year, or the first twelve months from arrival): each month is withheld on the status recorded for it (art.46(3), art.64(4): income is taxed when paid), and a change of status during the year is settled in the annual finalisation, which re-prices the year’s wage income on the resident table and credits what was withheld at 20% (art.51; Decree 126/2020 art.8(6)(d)); earlier months are never re-withheld. Leave cash-out: art.26(2) exempts the pay for untaken leave only within the Labour Code art.113(3) conditions and rate (the Decree 145/2020 art.67(3) day), and art.26(3) taxes the excess; income is taxed in the month it is paid (art.46(3)), so an excess is income of the paying month and is never spread over earlier periods. Meal: Decree 253/2026 art.8(2)(g) with art.69(1)(b) — from 1 July 2026 a meal paid by the employer is taxable only above 1,200,000 a month; a meal served in kind is not income. A class counting toward PIT.MEAL enters the base only above that cap. Housing: rent, power and water the employer pays on the worker’s behalf is taxable at the amount paid but not above 15% of the worker’s other taxable income at the unit (Decree 253/2026 art.8(2)(h)); a class counting toward PIT.HOUSING enters at the lower of the two. Voluntary pension and life insurance: deducted as paid, at most 3,000,000 a month in total including the employer’s share, from tax year 2026 (Decree 253/2026 art.46(2)(a) with art.69(1)(a)), read from the dated VOLUNTARY_PENSION deduction claims; the annual settlement allows twelve months’ cap. The art.49 medical, education and charity deductions are not withheld monthly: a taxpayer who claims them settles with the tax office personally (Decree 253/2026 art.51(3)), so the employer never applies them. Year-end: the December re-pricing on the annual table is the employer’s finalisation, which it may make only for an employee who authorised it and qualifies (Decree 126/2020 art.8(6)(d); Decree 253/2026 art.51(2)): the PIT election `finalisation_authorised`. Without it December is withheld on the monthly table. Night work: Decree 253/2026 art.26(1) exempts "tiền lương, tiền công làm việc ban đêm" — the wage for night work itself, where Circular 111/2013 art.3(1)(i) exempted only "phần tiền lương, tiền công trả cao hơn" the day wage; Decree 145/2020 art.56 prices the night-work wage as the ordinary hour × night hours plus at least 30% of it. The ordinary night hours' share of the salary (`NIGHT_WAGE`) leaves the base beside the premium for every employee.

( this sentence gave the 1% of the superseded Decision 1908/QĐ-TLĐ art.23, which no version here applies.) The `union_member` election says who is one. Law 41/2024/QH15 art.31(1)(b) with Decree 158/2025/NĐ-CP art.7(1)(a)–(c): the insurance salary is the monthly job or title wage, plus the wage allowances and the other supplements of a stated amount agreed in the contract and paid regularly and stably each pay period, excluding items that depend on or vary with productivity, work history or performance (`terms.fixed_allowances`, the standing rows marked fixed); a row marked not fixed stays outside. Circular 06/2021/TT-BLĐTBXH, cited here before, was repealed from 1 July 2025 by Circular 12/2025/TT-BNV art.20(2)(b). Quyết định 61/QĐ-TLĐ of the Vietnam General Confederation of Labour, in force from 1 July 2025, cut the dues of a member in an enterprise outside the State sector to 0.5% of the salary the compulsory social insurance is based on, capped at 10% of the base salary (mức lương cơ sở) — the 1% of Decision 1908/QĐ-TLĐ no longer stands on any version here. https://pbgdpl.cantho.gov.vn/quyet-dinh-61qd-tld-ve-dieu-chinh-giam-muc-dong-doan-phi-cong-doan https://nhandan.vn/chinh-thuc-giam-muc-dong-doan-phi-cong-doan-tu-172025-post898504.html [DEC61] art.1 (city-portal transcription) waives dues only for a member on SI benefit for a month or more, or without work, income or pay for a month or more — not for the 14 unpaid working days that end the month’s SI contribution (Law 41/2024 art.33(5)); such a member still pays 0.5% of the insurance salary (the contractual salary and fixed supplements within the reference-level floor and ceiling). A member outside compulsory SI pays a set sum of at least 0.5% of the base salary; the union sets it, and the seed charges that minimum, 0.5% of 2530000.0. Owner rule 2026-09-28 (law silent on a part month): the waiver applies to a pay month in which every scheduled working day is wholly unpaid; maternity-benefit months stay waived as SI’s own exemption. [DEC61] art.1 waives dues only for a member on SI benefit for a month or more. A month with SI nil is now waived as a benefit month only for a birth, adoption, surrogate-birth or commissioning-mother maternity spell (the categories whose whole leave the SI rule already exempts by `maternity_category`; a birth spell is months long); a paternity spell (at most 14 working days, art.53(2)) or a short maternity event (miscarriage, check-up, contraception) no longer waives the dues, which fall on the insurance salary unless every scheduled working day of the month is wholly unpaid (fund-paid benefit days are wholly unpaid days on the payslip). Decree 135/2020/NĐ-CP art.4 with Annex I (signed text https://datafiles.chinhphu.vn/cpp/files/vbpq/2020/11/135.signed.pdf pp.1–3, read visually) sets the retirement age by the month and year of birth — the age of the year in which the worker reaches it (a man born 7/1964 retires at 61y3m in 10/2025) — so the foreign-worker retirement exclusion compares the age at signing with the Annex I age for `employee.birth_date`, not with the age of the signing year. Engine: members only — 0.5% of the insurance salary, at most 253,000 (10% of the reference level). Membership is the UNION_DUES election union_member (scheme.elections.union_member); a non-member is never charged. In a State-owned enterprise (entity fact state_owned_enterprise) the dues are 0.5% of the take-home salary after SI, HI, UI and PIT, same cap (Decision 61/QĐ-TLĐ); the scheme is assessed after PIT for that reason. Engine (round 7): on the contractual SI salary; a member outside compulsory SI pays the minimum 0.5% of the reference level (Decision 61/QĐ-TLĐ). The month's contribution is charged with the month's regular pay (re-verification 3, 2026-10-22): an off-cycle slip paid before the salary run pays no wage this scheme assesses and charges nothing, so a small bonus or claim slip is never consumed by the month's insurance. The phone, stationery, travel and uniform support (WORK_EXPENSE_ALLOWANCE) is a welfare support outside the insurance salary (Circular 10/2020/TT-BLĐTBXH art.3(5)(c); Official Letter 1198/CTL&BHXH-BHXH of 2025 under Decree 158/2025/NĐ-CP art.7), as its counts_toward already says.

  ?base.amount
  :terms.base_salary
  +sum(
    terms.allowances.filter(
      a,
      !(a.code
      in [
        "MEAL_ALLOWANCE",
        "HOUSING",
        "INSURANCE_EQUIVALENT",
        "WORK_EXPENSE_ALLOWANCE"
      ]
    ) ).map(
      a,
      double(a.amount)
    )
  )
